items.prompt: Black to move. White's knight has just taken f7 and attacks your queen and your rook. Find the reply.

claims.statement: Qxg2 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Black stands at least four pawns better (White's point of view, depth 16).
After Qxg2 the black queen attacks the rook on h1.

hints: Your queen is attacked, but a move that makes a bigger threat may beat running away.
Look at the white pawn next to the rook that has not moved.
The queen takes the pawn on g2 and attacks the rook on h1.
items.explain: Qxg2 attacks the rook on h1 (checked), and the engine rates Black at least four pawns better (checked, depth 16). The knight capture on f7 was the lure.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just recaptured on b5. Find a quiet move that attacks two things at once.

claims.statement: Qf3 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
After Qf3 White stands at least three pawns better (White's point of view, depth 16).
After Qf3 the rook on a8 is loose: attacked and not defended.

hints: Black has pushed pawns and left the back rank thin.
Look along the long diagonal from f3 to a8.
The queen goes to f3.
items.explain: Qf3 attacks the rook on a8 along the long diagonal, and nothing defends the rook (checked). The engine rates White at least three pawns better (checked, depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. The pawn on b5 can be recaptured. Decide whether that is sure material or bait, and play your move.

claims.statement: Nf6, Bb7 and e6 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Recapturing on b5 is at least 200 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Ask what the recapture takes away from Black's back rank.
After the recapture, look at the long diagonal toward the rook on a8.
A developing move such as Nf6 avoids the problem.
items.explain: Recapturing on b5 allows Qf3, which attacks the rook on a8 (see the board before this item), and it is at least 200 centipawns worse than the best move (checked, depth 16). Nf6, Bb7 and e6 stay within 40 centipawns of the first choice (checked).

feedback_by_move.c6b5: Recapturing wins the pawn back, but White answers with a queen move that attacks the rook on a8; it is at least 200 centipawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Choose a good move.

claims.statement: Nxe4 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
The quiet Be7 is at least 100 centipawns worse than Nxe4 (depth 16).

hints: A pawn can be taken. Run the two questions.
Count the checks and captures White could answer with.
Take on e4 with the knight.
items.explain: Nxe4 is the engine's first choice, and the quiet Be7 is at least 100 centipawns worse (checked, depth 16). The rule of thumb holds here: when the capture survives the two questions, take the material.

items.prompt: Black to move. Choose a good move.

claims.statement: dxc6 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Declining with Nf6 is at least 400 centipawns worse (depth 16).

hints: A piece of yours has just been taken. What can recapture?
Two black pawns can take on c6; one is the better recapture.
Take with the d-pawn.
items.explain: dxc6 recaptures the bishop and is the engine's first choice; Nf6 is at least 400 centipawns worse (checked, depth 16). Declining a recapture is not caution, it leaves a piece lost.

items.prompt: White to move. Choose a good move.

claims.statement: Every legal move is a quiet move: nothing can be captured.
Be2, Be3, h3 and Bd3 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).

hints: Look at the board for something to take.
No white move captures anything, and your e-pawn is defended by the knight on c3.
Make a developing or useful quiet move.
items.explain: White has no capture available (every legal move is quiet, checked), so the capture-or-decline question does not arise. Be2, Be3, h3 and Bd3 are within 40 centipawns of the engine's first choice (checked, depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. Choose a good move.

claims.statement: Nxe5 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Taking the queen with Bxd1 is at least 1000 centipawns worse (depth 16): it walks into mate.

hints: The queen is on offer. Before you take it, look for White's best check.
After Bxd1 the white bishop has a check on f7; follow it to the end.
Take the knight with the knight.
items.explain: Nxe5 wins a piece and is the engine's first choice, while Bxd1 takes the queen but walks into Bxf7+ Ke7 and a knight mate on d5 (checked, at least 1000 centipawns worse, depth 16). It is the lure of the first board, with a knight on c6 instead of a pawn on g6.

feedback_by_move.g4d1: Taking the queen runs into a check on f7 and a knight mate on d5; it is at least 1000 centipawns worse.

items.prompt: White to move. Taking on e5 right now loses to the bishop taking the queen. Find the developing move that makes that capture a trap next turn.

claims.statement: After Nc3 g6 Nxe5 Bxd1 Bxf7+ Ke7, Nd5 is checkmate.
Taking on e5 at once is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which piece must stand on c3 for the final knight jump?
Do not take on e5 yet.
Play the knight from b1 to c3.
items.explain: With the knight on c3, the line Nxe5 Bxd1 Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5 is mate (checked). Taking at once, with the knight still on b1, is at least 300 centipawns worse (checked, depth 16). The lure works only after the quiet developing move.

feedback_by_move.f3e5: Taking at once fails: no knight stands on c3, so the mating jump to d5 is missing.

items.prompt: White to move. Taking on e5 now would allow a queen check on h4. Find a quiet move that keeps the chance without risking material.

claims.statement: d3, Nc3 and Be2 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Taking on e5 at once is at least 20 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The queen check is the problem. What would stop it?
A quiet developing move keeps everything protected.
Play d3, Nc3 or Be2.
items.explain: d3, Nc3 and Be2 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's first choice (checked, depth 16), and taking on e5 at once is at least 20 centipawns worse (checked). Make the capture safe first, then take.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's knight stands on b1, not c3. May Black take the queen now? Play your move.

claims.statement: Bxd1 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
The white knight is on b1.

hints: Compare with the first board: which white piece is missing from c3?
Follow the white bishop check to the end.
Without the knight on c3 there is no mating jump, so take the queen.
items.explain: Bxd1 is the engine's first choice (checked): with the knight on b1 the mating jump to d5 is missing, so the check on f7 only wins a pawn and a knight for White. Same lure, one piece moved, opposite verdict.
